biggest_catch: It's a monthly discount on your phone or internet bill — up to $9.25/month ($34.25 on Tribal lands) — not cash you can spend anywhere. One benefit per household, and you must re-qualify every year or you lose it.
catches: One Lifeline benefit per household — if anyone in your household already gets it, you can't get a second one.
It's a service discount, not cash: it lowers your bill with a participating provider.
You must recertify eligibility every year; fail to recertify and the benefit is removed.
You must stay enrolled with a participating phone or broadband provider; not every carrier offers it.
Income limit is 135% of federal poverty guidelines, or participation in a qualifying assistance program (SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, etc.).

c1.evidence: The FCC is the federal regulator that administers Lifeline; the program is described on fcc.gov.

c2.evidence: Official FCC consumer page states the benefit: up to $9.25/month discount on phone or broadband service, up to $34.25/month on Tribal lands.

c3.evidence: No fee to enroll or participate; the benefit is a discount applied to service.

c4.evidence: Official page states the monthly discount amounts; the discount is applied to the monthly bill by the participating provider.

eligibility: Household income at or below 135% of federal poverty guidelines, OR a household member participates in a qualifying assistance program (e.g., SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, Federal Public Housing Assistance). One benefit per household. Annual recertification required.
notes: Verified from the official FCC Lifeline consumer page on 2026-09-23. Amounts ($9.25/month standard; $34.25/month Tribal lands) confirmed on the official page. Framed as bill savings, not cash income. Apply through a participating provider or the National Verifier.
payout_quote: Lifeline provides a discount of up to $9.25 per month on phone or broadband service (up to $34.25 per month on Tribal lands) for eligible low-income households.

s1.note: One benefit per household; income or program participation required; annual recertification.

s2.note: No enrollment fee; the discount only exists as long as you stay with a participating provider and recertify.

s3.note: Discount applies to the monthly bill on an ongoing basis while eligible.

s4.note: Amounts stated flatly on the official page — no qualifying weasel words on the core benefit.

s5.note: https://www.fcc.gov/lifeline-consumers — the official FCC consumer page.

s6.note: Steps are concrete: check eligibility, pick a participating provider, apply, recertify yearly.

steps: Confirm you qualify: household income at or below 135% of federal poverty guidelines, or someone in your household is on SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, or another qualifying program.
Pick a phone or broadband provider in your area that participates in Lifeline (the FCC page links to provider lookup).
Apply — either directly through the provider or via the National Verifier at lifelinesupport.org if your state requires it.
Once approved, the discount (up to $9.25/month; up to $34.25 on Tribal lands) is applied to your monthly bill.
Recertify your eligibility every year to keep the benefit — set a reminder so it doesn't lapse.
timing: Monthly discount applied to your bill for as long as you remain eligible and recertified.
